summary: The note spotlights how schools across a local district have integrated technology since September 2023, from digital classrooms and one-to-one laptops to coding classes, virtual field trips, a digital media center, digital citizenship lessons, adaptive tech for special needs, and teacher workshops. It also covers community support such as TechBridge's sponsorship of a citywide STEM fair in April 2024. The note frames these efforts as an ongoing journey that still depends on skilled teaching.
one_line: Local schools have adopted digital tools since September 2023, with new programs at many campuses and community backing, as part of an ongoing journey to bridge the digital divide.
key_facts: Maple Grove Elementary School unveiled new digital classrooms on September 15, 2023, equipped with smart boards, tablets, and educational apps.
Principal Linda Harris of Maple Grove Elementary said bridging the digital divide gives all students a fair chance at success and that digital literacy is a necessity.
Valley High School launched a one-to-one program on October 9, 2023, giving each student a personal laptop; sophomore Jason DeLuca said it means he can work on projects from anywhere.
Jefferson Middle School has offered coding classes since December 2023, led by computer science teacher Benjamin Thomas, to foster problem-solving skills and creativity.
Oakwood Elementary began a 'Tech Tuesdays' program in early January 2024 with virtual field trips to museums, historical sites, and science labs, championed by fourth-grade teacher Emily Rodriguez.
In March 2024 Central Middle School converted its library into a digital media center with e-books, audio libraries, and interactive learning stations, spearheaded by librarian John Carter.
Riverview High School started its Digital Citizenship program in November 2023, teaching online safety, ethics, and digital footprint; media specialist Sarah Morrison leads it.

Franklin Elementary has used adaptive technology tailored to individual needs since the start of the 2023/2024 school year; special education teacher Michael Johnson said technology can give a voice to those who struggle to communicate.
Willow Creek High School launched professional development workshops for teachers starting February 2024; history teacher Laura Smith attended a digital storytelling workshop.
In April 2024, technology firm TechBridge sponsored a citywide STEM fair where students showcased tech projects.
TechBridge CEO Marcus O'Connell said investing in education technology is investing in the future.
The note stresses that digital learning also underlines the vitality of skilled teaching and continuous evolution in educational practices.
